title: Working From Home (עבודה מהבית)
text: When remote work became common, many people expected it to be a temporary arrangement. Instead, it reshaped how companies think about offices altogether. Employees gained flexibility and saved hours of commuting, yet some struggled to separate their work from their personal lives. The challenge now is not whether to work remotely, but how to do it well.

questions.explanation: 'not whether... but how to do it well'.

title: The Price of Convenience (מחיר הנוחות)
text: Same-day delivery feels almost magical: you order something in the morning and it arrives by evening. But that speed comes at a cost. Behind it lies a network of warehouses, drivers under pressure, and packaging that often ends up as waste. Convenience is rarely free — someone, somewhere, pays for it.

title: The Return of Vinyl (שובם של התקליטים)
text: In an age of instant streaming, the comeback of vinyl records seems strange. Yet sales have grown for over a decade. For many listeners, the appeal is not sound quality but ritual: choosing a record, placing the needle, and listening to a whole album without skipping. In a world of endless choice, limits can feel like a relief.

options: Its comeback in a streaming age

questions.question: What is the main appeal, per the text?
questions.explanation: 'the appeal is not sound quality but ritual'.

title: Why We Procrastinate (למה אנחנו דוחים)
text: Procrastination is often blamed on laziness, but psychologists see it differently. Putting off a task is usually a way to avoid an uncomfortable feeling — boredom, anxiety, or fear of failure. Understanding this changes the solution: instead of forcing more discipline, we can make the first step smaller and less frightening.

questions.question: How do psychologists explain procrastination?
questions.explanation: 'a way to avoid an uncomfortable feeling'.

title: The Language of Silence (שפת השתיקה)
text: We tend to think communication is about words, but silence carries meaning too. A pause before answering can signal thought, doubt, or respect, depending on the culture. In some societies, silence in conversation is comfortable and normal; in others, it creates anxiety and people rush to fill it. Misreading these signals is a common source of misunderstanding.

title: The Attention Economy (כלכלת הקשב)
text: Many free apps are not really free; we pay with our attention. Their business depends on keeping us scrolling, because more time means more advertising revenue. Recognising this does not mean we must delete everything, but it does mean using these tools deliberately rather than letting them use us.

title: Failure as Data (כישלון כמידע)
text: In many successful companies, failure is not punished but studied. A failed experiment is treated as information: it rules out one path and points toward better ones. This mindset is hard to adopt because failure feels personal, yet teams that learn to separate the result from their self-worth tend to improve fastest.

title: The Myth of Multitasking (מיתוס ריבוי המשימות)
text: We pride ourselves on multitasking, yet research suggests the brain does not truly do two demanding things at once. Instead, it switches rapidly between tasks, and each switch carries a hidden cost in time and accuracy. What feels efficient is often slower and more error-prone than simply doing one thing at a time.

questions.explanation: 'a hidden cost in time and accuracy'.

title: The Cost of Free (המחיר של חינם)
text: A 'free' trial that quietly turns into a paid subscription relies on one thing: that we forget to cancel. Companies know our intentions are weak and our calendars are full. The lesson isn't cynicism but a small habit — set a reminder the moment you sign up, before the convenience makes you forget.

options: Set a reminder when you sign up
questions.explanation: 'set a reminder the moment you sign up'.

title: Open-Plan Offices (משרדים פתוחים)
text: Open-plan offices were sold as a way to boost collaboration. In practice, studies suggest they often do the opposite: people put on headphones, send more messages, and talk face-to-face less. Removing walls, it turns out, can build invisible ones.

title: The Expert and the Crowd (המומחה וההמון)
text: For certain questions, the averaged guess of a large crowd can beat the lone expert — a phenomenon known as the wisdom of crowds. But it has a catch: it works only when people decide independently. Once they start copying one another, the crowd grows confident and wrong at the same time.

questions.explanation: 'confident and wrong at the same time'.

title: The Skill of Saying No (האומנות של לומר לא)
text: Many of us say yes too easily — to favours, meetings, and projects — and then resent the lack of time we are left with. Learning to decline politely is not selfish; it is what makes our yes meaningful. A calendar full of reluctant agreements helps no one.

title: Reading the Reviews (לקרוא את הביקורות)
text: Online reviews feel democratic, but they are easily skewed. The very happy and the very angry are far more likely to post than the quietly satisfied majority. A wise reader looks past the star rating to the patterns: recurring complaints matter more than a single furious paragraph.

title: The Tyranny of the New (עריצות החדש)
text: We treat 'new' as a synonym for 'better', upgrading devices and habits at the first opportunity. Yet much of what endures does so because it has quietly passed thousands of tests we never see. Before discarding the old, it's worth asking what problem the new version actually solves — and whether we had that problem at all.

title: Disagreeing Well (להתווכח כמו שצריך)
text: The goal of an argument should be to get closer to the truth, not to win. That sounds obvious, yet most disagreements quickly become contests of ego. The most useful question you can ask isn't 'How is he wrong?' but 'What would he have to be right about for his view to make sense?'
